statement: The function returns a result vector r such that: (1) for every i with 0 <= i < len(r), r[i] is a stepping number and low <= r[i] <= high, where a nonnegative integer n is stepping iff, in its base-10 representation without leading zeros (with n = 0 written as the single digit 0), every pair of adjacent digits has absolute difference exactly 1; (2) for every integer x, x occurs in r if and only if low <= x <= high and x is stepping; (3) for every i, j with 0 <= i < j < len(r), r[i] <= r[j]; (4) for every i, j with 0 <= i < len(r), 0 <= j < len(r), and i != j, r[i] != r[j].
preconditions: The arguments low and high, viewed as mathematical integers, satisfy 0 <= low <= high <= 2000000000.
